report: Independent shadow convergence review of PR #2026 (issue #2024: enforce workpad size limits before a write). The change adds two byte-measured guards to scripts/workpad.py: a 2,048-byte per-note budget on caller-supplied --note/--note-file text (_check_note_within_budget, iterated over _own_notes BEFORE the buffer-replay fold in cmd_update, so tool-composed rows and buffer-replayed notes are exempt), and a 65,536-byte comment-body limit before any PATCH (_check_body_within_limit, called pre-PATCH in cmd_update at ~line 3642 and inside _patch_comment_body for both the in-memory text branch via _byte_len and the body_path branch via stat().st_size). Refused writes exit non-zero before the failed-write buffer, so nothing is replayed. Both PATCH routes and the byte-vs-character conservativeness are correct and fail-closed. The two prior-round fixes are reconciled: AC10 now covers _patch_comment_body's body-path route directly (test_python_scripts.py ~2664-2678) and the operand-trace mandate rewrite (multi-row table -> one --note per comparand) is mirrored consistently across skills/implement/references/sweep-2-3-0c-operand-trace.md, skills/implement/phases/phase-2-implement.md, and docs/internal/implement-skill.md. Coupled assertion floors (run.sh + workflow-flight-recorder-registry.json minimum_assertions, exact policy) and coverage-map.json are updated in lockstep. All five dispatched reviewers converged with no Critical or Important findings. Remaining items are Suggestion/Minor: cmd_create is not size-guarded (out of issue scope; fails loud at the API), AC7 tests only 1 of 5 exempt tool-composed row types (exemption mechanism is uniform), the several-within-budget-notes-jointly-over-cap interaction case is untested, the update-route exact 65536 boundary is untested, and the changeset's anti-wedge claim is accurate for the per-note budget but narrower than it reads with respect to the inherent comment-cap wedge (explicitly out of scope per the issue). Verdict: APPROVE, merge-ready pending the standard CI required-check pass.

phase3_findings.description: AC7: only the `checkpoint` tool-composed exempt row is tested; the other four named types (review-coverage, scope-decision, deferred-filed, completion-verification) have no oversize-exemption assertion (test_python_scripts.py:2617-2620)
Named residual untested: several individually within-budget notes whose assembled body jointly exceeds the 65,536-byte comment cap (the per-note-pass / body-cap-fires interaction path)

cmd_create (scripts/workpad.py:1374) posts the initial --body-file with no _check_body_within_limit guard; the one comment-writing route not covered, though it fails loud at the GitHub 422 and is outside issue #2024's PATCH-scoped wording

The changeset anti-wedge claim ("a note that predated this change can no longer wedge a workpad") holds for the per-note budget but not for accumulated buffered content pushing the assembled body past the comment cap; not a regression (identical pre-change), but the claim reads broader than it is (.changeset/issue-2024-workpad-size-limits.md:10-11)

Off-by-one: the exact 65,536-byte boundary is asserted only on the patch route (test_python_scripts.py:2678); the cmd_update route tests only a gross over-cap body, so a >= vs > slip in the update-route guard would not be caught. Note budget lower edge (2047) also untested
AC4 body-refusal test (test_python_scripts.py:2597) asserts '65536' and 'byte count' are present but not the measured body byte-count value, unlike the note path which asserts '2049 bytes'

_check_note_within_budget / _check_body_within_limit docstrings trail a design-rationale clause already carried verbatim by the adjacent call-site inline comments (borderline mirror-fact restatement under §2.3.4a); _byte_len docstring restates its one-line body
AC11 note-refusal assertion depends on the digit-string '700' never appearing in the refusal message (substring-brittle, fine today)
